October 3, 2026

Trump administration sends pre-midterm checks to seniors and Obamacare enrollees

tags: politics, economy
sources: @aaronparnas

The administration is sending $100 checks to more than 20 million seniors, which it says will help cover Medicare Part B premiums and will be drawn from a Medicare Improvement Fund, with delivery expected in the coming weeks. That follows $500 Obamacare refund checks going to nearly a million Americans, concentrated in battleground states. Trump has also said every American, including children, would receive a $5,000 check if Republicans win the November midterms. Critics have characterised the payments as an effort to bribe voters ahead of the election.

Justice Department drops cases protecting disabled Americans' right to live in their communities

tags: politics, legal, health
sources: @aaronparnas

NBC News reported that the Justice Department has begun abandoning cases that protect the rights of disabled people to live in community settings, following an earlier administration memo that withdrew federal support from community-based housing and services and expanded institutionalisation of homeless people. At least five investigations have been abandoned or weakened since the memo was issued. In Florida, the department is seeking to roll back a court order it previously won to keep medically fragile children out of nursing homes. In Texas, it is walking away from a 16-year lawsuit aimed at helping disabled people live in their communities.

Nearly 200 quarantined in Siberia after reported pneumonic plague death

tags: health, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Nearly 200 people are under observation in Siberia, Russia, after one person died from what appears to be pneumonic plague, according to the Moscow Times and author Annie Jacobsen. The cases are reported to be linked to a BSL-3 laboratory, and local Russian outlets say authorities are treating the situation seriously. Residents describe masks being distributed in kindergartens and people in protective suits on the streets. No cases have been linked to the United States, and the full scope is unclear given limited information coming out of Russia.

Trump posts Senator Tom Cotton's personal phone number over daylight saving vote

tags: politics, privacy
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump published Senator Tom Cotton's cell phone number in a Truth Social post attacking the Arkansas Republican for declining to support the Sunshine Protection Act, which would make daylight saving time permanent. The post included a lengthy criticism of Cotton, a longtime ally of the president. Cotton's mailbox was reported full and calls went to voicemail following the post. No comment from Cotton has been issued.

Trump attacks Letitia James over appointment as special prosecutor in Cornell case

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump said he feels badly for the seven Cornell fraternity members accused of drugging and gang-raping a student, arguing they will not get a "fair shake" now that New York Attorney General Letitia James has been appointed special prosecutor for the investigation. He called James "a corrupt person" in remarks about the case. Trump was previously found liable for sexually abusing E. Jean Carroll and ordered to pay millions of dollars in damages.

Report finds Cornell imposed minor sanctions in most sexual misconduct cases

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

A USA Today investigation found that more than 1,200 incidents of sexual assault, dating and domestic violence and stalking were reported to Cornell University's Title IX office between 2018 and 2024. Cornell filed disciplinary charges against an accused student in 162 of those cases and found at least one student at fault in 51. Most of those found responsible received minor sanctions such as probation or training that allowed them to remain on campus, with 14 suspensions and seven expulsions or dismissals. The findings come amid allegations against seven fraternity members accused of assaulting a student.

Texas industry groups warn tomato tariffs could end free chips and salsa

tags: economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

The Texas International Produce Association and the Texas Restaurant Association warned that rising tomato prices are making it too costly for restaurants to continue offering free chips and salsa. The groups pointed to the 17% tariff imposed on Mexican tomatoes last year, alongside poor growing weather in states such as Florida. Restaurants have absorbed the cost so far but may begin charging customers.
